# Results — Study 811 (Zero-Return Illiquidity)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test —
Lesmond, Ogden & Trzcinka (1999): the **proportion of trailing days with an exactly-zero
daily return** is a transaction-cost / illiquidity proxy, and illiquid names should earn
an **illiquidity premium**, so a long-high-zero / short-low-zero book should earn a
positive spread. Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to
reproduce every number. As-of **2026-06-30** (the last complete calendar month; the
partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `357fd262912f` (panel Close).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily OHLC (`auto_adjust=True`, total-return), **50 liquid US large-caps**, 2010-01-04 → 2026-06-30, **4,147** dated rows/name |
| Universe | a fixed `UNIVERSE` of ~50 mega-caps, pulled through the **`quantlab.universe` survivorship guard** (`download_panel(..., allow_survivorship_bias=True)`), cached under this study's own `_cache/` |
| Signal | each name's **trailing-252-day proportion of exactly-zero daily returns** (`\|r\| < 1e-8`, the LOT proxy), known at the close of `t−1` (one `shift`) |
| Sort | each day rank the cross-section by the signal; **long the top 30%** (high zero = illiquid), **short the bottom 30%** (low zero = liquid), equal-weight; measure the day-`t` forward return of each book |
| Execution / costs | one documented lag: signal through close `t−1` → hold day `t`. The costed timer charges 2 sides × one-way cost × NAV per day on the long-short book; the short book pays 50 bps/yr borrow |
| Stamp | as-of 2026-06-30 (last complete calendar month; no partial month) — Fingerprint `357fd262912f` |
| Statistics | Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily spread; one-sample *t*; Welch *t* on the pooled illiquid-vs-liquid books; a 1,000-permutation placebo; a 20-seed synthetic positive control |

**Survivorship — named on the Signal axis.** `UNIVERSE` is a **current-membership** list of
names that are liquid mega-caps *today*, so the magnitudes are an **upper bound**. It also
sharpens the central caveat below: a mega-cap survivor set is the single *worst* place to
look for an illiquidity premium, because these names are exactly the ones that never sit
still.

## The signal is near-degenerate on this universe

The trailing-252-day zero-return proportion on the final row of the panel:

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| minimum across names | **0.00%** of days |
| median across names | **0.00%** of days |
| maximum across names | **2.38%** of days |
| long-book (top-30%) trailing zero-proportion, time-averaged | **~1.38%** of days |

Half the mega-caps never print an exactly-zero adjusted daily return over a trailing year;
the "liquid" short leg is a tie-broken pile of names sitting at exactly **0.00%**. There is
barely any cross-sectional signal to sort on — the LOT proxy is built for the tick-priced
small-cap tape, not for 50 mega-caps. This is the honest reason to expect **None** before we
even look at the returns.

## The headline — long-high-zero / short-low-zero spread

Daily equal-weight top-30% minus bottom-30% zero-proportion spread (n = **3,894** days,
median 50 names/day):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| **spread (long illiquid − short liquid)** | **−1.37 bps/day** |
| Newey-West(10) *t* | **−1.29** |
| one-sample *t* | −1.29 |
| illiquid book / liquid book | +6.55 bps / +7.93 bps (Welch *t* = −0.52) |
| gross spread Sharpe (no cost) | −0.33 |

The claimed illiquidity premium **is absent.** The spread is a statistically insignificant
**−1.37 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−1.29**, |t| < 2): the high-zero "illiquid" names did not
out-earn — if anything they very mildly *under*-earned, but not significantly. On a
50-mega-cap survivor panel where the proxy is near-degenerate, there is simply nothing to
harvest.

## Placebo — is even the small tilt a lucky alignment of the sort?

Keep the trailing zero-proportion sort but read each day's forward returns from a
**column-permuted** panel (signal → outcome link broken), 1,000 permutations (20 seeds × 50):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| observed spread | **−1.37 bps** |
| placebo mean (sd) | +0.123 bps (1.108) |
| position of observed | ≈ **1.35σ into the left tail** (right-tail p = 0.907) |

The permutation null centres at zero; the observed −1.37 bps sits barely more than one sigma
away — comfortably inside the noise band. Nothing to see, in either direction.

## Robustness — two eras (split 2018-01-01)

| era | spread | NW *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 2010-01 → 2018-01 (n=1,760) | −2.23 bps | **−1.69** |
| 2018-01 → 2026-06 (n=2,134) | −0.66 bps | **−0.41** |

Neither era clears |t| ≥ 2; the (weakly negative) tilt is not stable and not significant —
consistent with a null.

## The timer — can you get paid for it?

Charge 2 sides × one-way × NAV per day on the long-short book; short pays 50 bps/yr borrow.

| one-way cost | gross/day | cost/day | net/day | *t* (net) | Sharpe (net) | ~ann. |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **1 bp** | −1.37 bps | 2.14 bps | **−3.51 bps** | −3.30 | −0.84 | −8.8%/yr |
| **5 bps** | −1.37 bps | 10.14 bps | **−11.51 bps** | −10.83 | −2.76 | −29.0%/yr |

The book loses money gross, and any friction only digs the hole deeper. And the costs quoted
here are *optimistic*: the long leg is by construction the least-liquid names, where a 1 bp
one-way is a fantasy floor. **Mirage.**

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded panel: each name carries a latent illiquidity `q_i` that sets its
zero-return frequency and (with `edge>0`) lifts its forward mean — the planted illiquidity
premium. No network.

| world | spread NW *t* |
|---|--:|
| null (`edge = 0`), **20 seeds** | mean **−0.67** (sd 0.88), **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/20 seeds** |
| planted (`edge = 0.012`, seed 811) | **+11.23** (Welch *t* = +10.98) |

The detector recovers a *planted* illiquidity premium cleanly and never fires on the null —
so the flat real-tape result is a true absence of the effect on the mega-cap universe, not a
broken sort. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in support of the real-tape
stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The Lesmond-Ogden-Trzcinka zero-return illiquidity premium does **not**
  appear on 50 liquid US mega-caps. The long-high-zero / short-low-zero spread is
  **−1.37 bps/day** (NW *t* = **−1.29**, |t| < 2) — insignificant, weakly wrong-signed, and
  not stable across eras (*t* = −1.69 / −0.41). The proxy is near-degenerate here (median
  trailing zero-proportion **0.00%**), exactly as the illiquidity literature predicts for a
  mega-cap universe: the effect lives in small, tick-priced names, not among mega-caps that
  never sit still.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The book loses money gross (−1.37 bps/day) and worse net
  (−3.51 bps/day at 1 bp, −11.51 at 5 bps); and the long leg's real trading costs are far
  above the optimistic floor charged here.
